draft.title: Titration curves
card: A titration curve is a graph of pH (vertical axis) against the volume of solution added from the burette (horizontal axis). It shows how the pH of the flask changes during a titration.
The curve has a steep, near vertical section. The equivalence point is the midpoint of this section, where the acid and base have reacted in exactly the amounts shown by the balanced equation.

For a strong acid and a strong base, the equivalence point is at pH 7 at 25°C. For a weak acid titrated with a strong base, it is above 7, because the conjugate base of the weak acid makes the solution basic.
A weak acid curve also has a flatter buffer region before the steep section. Here the flask holds both the weak acid and its conjugate base, so the pH changes only slowly as base is added.
draft.remember: The equivalence point is the middle of the steep rise. A weak acid curve also has a flat buffer region before it.

a.q: On a titration curve, which part shows the equivalence point?
opts: The midpoint of the steep, near vertical section
The starting pH before any solution is added
The end of the graph at the largest volume added
The middle of the flat region before the steep rise
a.why: At the equivalence point the acid and base have reacted in exactly the amounts in the balanced equation, and the pH changes sharply around it. The flat region before the rise is the buffer region of a weak acid, where the pH changes slowly.
a.clue: Look for where the pH jumps most for a tiny volume.

b.q: Ethanoic acid (a weak acid) is titrated with sodium hydroxide (a strong base). Why is the pH at the equivalence point above 7?
opts: The ethanoate ion formed is a weak base
Sodium hydroxide is added in excess at that point
Ethanoic acid is not fully used up at that point
The salt formed is always neutral in water
b.why: At equivalence all the ethanoic acid has reacted to form ethanoate ions. These are the conjugate base of a weak acid and react with water to make the solution basic. Excess sodium hydroxide is only present after the equivalence point, so it does not explain this pH.
b.clue: Think about what is in the flask once all the weak acid has reacted.

a.best: The midpoint of the steep, near vertical section

b.best: The ethanoate ion formed is a weak base
